html:
The French translation of the Thousand and One Nights by the scholar Antoine Galland, published in twelve volumes from 1704 to 1717. It brought the tales of Shahrazad to Europe.

Galland had travelled in the Ottoman Empire as a diplomat's secretary and collector. His main source was a Syrian manuscript of the late Middle Ages. To fill more volumes he added stories that are not in any older Arabic copy of the Nights, among them Aladdin and Ali Baba. Many of these were told to him in Paris in 1709 by Hanna Diyab, a young Maronite Christian traveller from Aleppo. Galland also freely smoothed the tales to suit French taste.

The books were a huge success and were soon translated into English and other languages. They set off a fashion for Eastern tales and shaped how Europeans imagined the Middle East for centuries, for good and ill. The writer Jorge Luis Borges suggested that Romanticism began with them. In turn, the European fame of the Nights later gave the stories new status in the Arab world too.
sum: The French translation of the Thousand and One Nights by the scholar Antoine Galland, published in twelve volumes from 1704 to 1717. It brought the tales of Shahrazad to Europe.
